sub_unit_name: Biodegradable polymers: Concept and advantages - Polylactic acid and Polyvinyl alcohol and their applications

content.title: Biodegradable Polymers
content.description: Biodegradable polymers are polymers that can be decomposed into harmless substances such as water, carbon dioxide, and biomass by the action of microorganisms under suitable environmental conditions.

content.content: Unlike conventional plastics, biodegradable polymers reduce environmental pollution because they naturally degrade after use. They are increasingly used in medical, packaging, and agricultural applications.

content.title: Engineering Importance
content.content: Biodegradable polymers help reduce plastic waste and promote sustainable development by replacing non-degradable plastics in many applications.

Biodegradable polymers are designed to break down naturally through the action of bacteria, fungi, and other microorganisms. The degradation products are generally non-toxic and environmentally friendly.

items.question: Eco-Friendly
items.answer: Reduce environmental pollution caused by plastic waste.

items.question: Renewable Sources
items.answer: Many are produced from renewable agricultural resources.

items.question: Medical Safety
items.answer: Suitable for biomedical and pharmaceutical applications.

content.content: Polylactic Acid (PLA) is a biodegradable polyester prepared from lactic acid obtained from renewable resources such as corn starch and sugarcane. It possesses good strength, transparency, and biodegradability.

rows: Food packaging, disposable cups, sutures, 3D printing

content.content: Polyvinyl Alcohol (PVA) is a water-soluble synthetic polymer prepared by the hydrolysis of polyvinyl acetate. It exhibits excellent film-forming ability, adhesion, flexibility, and biodegradability under suitable conditions.

rows: Water soluble, flexible, good film former
Packaging films, adhesives, textiles, paper coating

left_points: Used in packaging and biomedical fields
right_points: Used in films, textiles and coatings

content.content: Biodegradable polymers are widely used in food packaging, agricultural films, drug delivery systems, surgical sutures, disposable products, tissue engineering, biodegradable bags, paper coatings, adhesives, and environmentally friendly consumer products.

content.title: Exam Tip
content.content: Focus on the concept, advantages, preparation, properties, and applications of PLA and PVA. These are commonly asked in engineering chemistry examinations.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Biodegradable polymers decompose naturally by microorganisms.
PLA is prepared from lactic acid and used in packaging and biomedical products.
PVA is obtained from polyvinyl acetate and is water soluble.
Both polymers are important eco-friendly engineering materials.
